evidence.description: The task is stored on the instance and strongly binds self before entering the ongoing loop.
The only visible cancellation occurs during deinitialization.

candidates.explanation: Although the task initially captures self weakly, the guard promotes it to a strong reference before the entire timer loop. The instance retains the task, and the running task retains the instance. Cancellation is only performed in deinit, which this retention prevents from being reached for an otherwise unreferenced instance.
candidates.title: Timer task retains its owner indefinitely

evidence.description: The initial interval is calculated and assigned but never consumed.
A separate interval calculation supplies the sleep duration.

candidates.explanation: The initialInterval value is never read. This performs an unnecessary asynchronous Statistics access before the first publication, while the loop separately calculates the interval it actually uses.
candidates.title: Initial interval calculation is unused

evidence.description: The reciprocal calculation permits an infinite interval when the rate is zero.
The computed interval is converted directly to UInt64.
The floating-point projection is converted directly to Int.

candidates.explanation: The code converts computed floating-point values to integers without checking finiteness or representable range. In particular, a zero investment rate produces an infinite interval: the minimum bound imposed by max does not remove infinity, and converting the resulting sleep duration to UInt64 traps. The projected total is likewise converted to Int without a range check.
candidates.title: Unchecked floating-point conversions can trap

evidence.description: Related Statistics properties are read at separate suspension points.
All three independently read values are combined into one projection.

candidates.explanation: The rate, total, and last-updated timestamp are obtained through three separate awaited accesses. These accesses do not establish a coherent snapshot: Statistics can process updates between them, allowing the projection to combine values from different states.
candidates.title: Projection reads related actor state non-atomically
